title: Stop relying on find.byKey(...).last for time-row lookups in notifications_screen_l1_test.dart and notifications_screen_test.dart
why: _SettingsTimeRow (learning_tracker/lib/features/notifications/presentation/screens/notifications_screen.dart:306, `return ListTile(key: key, ...)`) forwards its own key onto the inner ListTile it builds, so Key('reminder_time')/Key('streak_alert_time') each match 2 elements in the tree. All 8 sites paper over that with `.last`, trusting find.byKey's traversal order to put the ListTile after its wrapper -- an implementation detail, not a documented Flutter API contract -- while the very same file already uses a robust, order-independent alternative for the Switch rows (e.g. l1_test.dart:218-220, `find.descendant(of: reminderRow, matching: find.byType(Switch))`). If the match order ever flipped, `.last` would silently resolve to the wrapper widget and the ensuing `tester.widget<ListTile>(...)` cast would throw, breaking otherwise-unrelated tests with a confusing error.
recommendation: Match the ListTile the same way the Switch rows already do -- e.g. `find.widgetWithText(ListTile, l10n.notifReminderTime)` or, on the production side, stop forwarding `key` to the inner ListTile in _SettingsTimeRow and instead expose a distinct key for it -- so the finder resolves to exactly one widget without depending on registration order.
acceptance_criteria: Time-row assertions no longer call `.last` on a byKey finder with 2 matches.
The 8 call sites are updated or, if `.last` is kept, each carries a comment justifying why the order is guaranteed.
